records.name_note: Sources split on the lead common name. NC State's rendered Common Name(s) list is alphabetized and begins with Brown-Eyed Susan (Thin Leaved Coneflower, Three-lobed Coneflower follow), and its Description prose opens with 'Brown-eyed Susan'. RHS's plant-profile common name is brown-eyed Susan, with three-leaved coneflower under Other common names. MoBot's single Common Name line reads three-leaved coneflower, while its Noteworthy Characteristics prose says the plant is commonly called brown-eyed Susan and lists thin-leaved coneflower and three-lobed coneflower as other names. NC State and MoBot both distinguish this plant from black-eyed Susan (R. hirta).
unknowns: toxic_to_pets / toxicity_detail: none of the three pages read (NC State, MoBot, RHS) names any toxicity, poison part, or Problem-for-Cats/Dogs tag for Rudbeckia triloba; no value taken from the genus or from R. hirta, so both are null.
is_edible: no page read addresses eating this plant. NC State's food source tags (herbage, nectar, pollen, fall, hard mast fruit) are wildlife tags, so is_edible is null (no record).

Life cycle, stated exactly: NC State's Description calls it an herbaceous biennial or short-lived perennial, its Life Cycle field lists Biennial and Perennial, and its Plant Type field lists four values (Ground Cover, Herbaceous Perennial, Native Plant, Wildflower). MoBot's Culture text says biennial or short-lived perennial, while its structured Type line says only Herbaceous perennial. RHS says short-lived perennial and tags it Herbaceous Perennial.

outdoor_sun_exposure: NC State's structured Light field also lists Partial Shade (2-6 hours) and its prose says it will grow in light shade, but MoBot's structured Sun field and RHS's Position field list full sun only (MoBot treats light shade as a tolerance in prose). part_shade is therefore left out.
direct_sun_hours_max: NC State's hour range comes only from its site-wide light legend, not species prose, so it is not used.
soil_ph_min / soil_ph_max: RHS gives pH as Acid or Alkaline or Neutral, which is categorical, and no page gives numeric bounds, so both are null.

water_regime and other watering fields: MoBot's structured Water field reads Medium, which is mid-scale and does not support keep_moist. No page frames watering as a dry-down pattern, and this is an in-ground perennial, so water_regime, water_dry_down_target, check depth and day-interval fields are null.

Size disagreement: NC State Dimensions give Height 3-5 ft and Width 1-1.5 ft (used). MoBot says Height 2.00 to 3.00 feet (prose: typically 2-3 ft, less frequently to 5 ft) and Spread 1.00 to 1.50 feet. RHS says Max Height 0.5-1 metres (19.7-39.4 in) and Max Spread 0.5-1 metres.

chill_damage_f, day/night temperatures, humidity, light foot-candles, fertilizing: not addressed by any page read. NC State lists USDA zones 4a-8b and MoBot zones 4 to 8, which are hardiness ratings, not damage onset temperatures.

Clemson HGIC, UF/IFAS, Penn State, UMD and UGA were not checked for a dedicated R. triloba page; no field depends on them. plantfinder.mobot.org may be skipped by the automated quote check because it refuses non-browser clients.

NC State's Problems field lists Contact Dermatitis and Weedy, and its tags include #contact dermatitis. RHS's Potentially harmful field says: "Sap can be a irritant. Wear gloves and other protective equipment when handling". The NC State page carries no Poison block and no Problem-for-Cats/Dogs tags.
unknowns: toxic_to_pets left null: no admissible source names cats or dogs for Sedum acre (NC State has no Poison block or Problem-for-Cats/Dogs tags; RHS and MoBot give no animal-specific toxicity).

Weedy and aggressive note: NC State says moss stonecrop 'spreads aggressively' and 'It can be weedy and aggressive in some situations', adding 'although it can overwhelm other plants of similar height', and its Problems field lists Weedy. RHS's Cultivation reads "May grow in a wide range of wello drainedsoils and be invasive." (typos as on the page).

is_edible is true only conditionally: NC State says stems and leaves can be eaten but large quantities can cause stomach upset; RHS does not address eating but flags irritant sap and NC State lists Contact Dermatitis; MoBot says "Specific epithet is named for its acrid taste." NC State also tags the species #children's garden and #playground plant.

outdoor_sun_exposure: NC State's structured Light field also lists Partial Shade and its prose says 'site for sun to part sun', and MoBot says 'Good tolerance for light shade', but MoBot's Sun field and RHS's Position are Full sun only, so part_sun/part_shade were left out.

soil_drainage moderate: NC State tags Good Drainage, Moist, Occasionally Dry and says avoid wet or poorly drained conditions; MoBot says tolerates moist (not wet) soils with good drainage; RHS says Moist but well-drained or Well-drained. No source describes it as wet-tolerant, but sources also do not describe sharp drainage only, so fast was not used.

water_regime dry_thoroughly_between is read from 'seldom needs watering' (NC State, MoBot); MoBot's structured Water field is 'Dry to medium'. No numeric watering interval or dry-down depth is given, so those fields are null.
soil_base is from NC State's container advice (coarse, well-drained, preferably a cactus mix); in the ground the sources describe sandy/shallow rocky, well-drained soil.
Soil pH: NC State lists Alkaline (>8.0) and Neutral (6.0-8.0) (open-ended band) and RHS lists Alkaline or Neutral, so no floor or ceiling was set.
chill_damage_f null: only hardiness zones given (NC State 3-9, MoBot 4-9 with culture text citing zones 3-8), not an onset temperature.
No admissible dedicated pages found for UF/IFAS, Clemson, PSU, UMD or UGA; no light foot-candle, humidity, temperature, or fertilizer data from admissible sources.

MoBot page was read at plantfinder.mobot.org and the www.missouribotanicalgarden.org URL redirects there. records.name_note: NC State's dedicated page is titled Euphorbia epithymoides. NC State says 'Much of the literature reports that Euphorbia polychroma is synonymous with Euphorbia epithymoides', but adds that according to POWO, E. epithymoides subsp. epithymoides is the synonym for Euphorbia polychroma, and its Cultivars / Varieties list carries 'Euphorbia epithymoides subsp. epithymoides (synonym--Euphorbia polychroma)'. NC State's Previously known as list gives Galarhoeus epithymoides, Pythius epithymoides and Tithymalus epithymoides. RHS's dedicated Euphorbia epithymoides page lists Euphorbia polychroma under Synonyms. Euphorbia epithymoides is kept as the accepted name because both dedicated pages file the plant under it; Euphorbia polychroma is the former name.
records.toxicity_detail: NC State's Poison block sits under the heading 'Poisonous to Humans', so its severity rating is human-scoped: Poison Severity: Low. Poison Symptoms: "The milky white latex sap found in all plant parts can cause mild to severe contact dermatitis. If contact with the eyes occurs the sap can cause temporary to permanent damage to the cornea. If eaten, blistering can occur on lips and oral mucosa. Avoid ingesting plant parts and keep plants away from pets and children." Poison Toxic Principle: Diterpene esters in milky latex. Causes Contact Dermatitis: Yes. Poison Part: Flowers, Fruits, Leaves, Sap/Juice, Stems. NC State's header statement "This plant has low severity poison characteristics." links to that block. Handling warning, from NC State's Description: "The milky sap is toxic to skin and eyes so be sure to wear gloves and eye protection when handling this plant. All parts of this plant are toxic if ingested. Monitor small children and pets." NC State's Edibility field: "Stems exude a slightly toxic, milky sap when cut." NC State's Problems field (separate from the Poison block) lists Contact Dermatitis, Poisonous to Humans, Problem for Cats, Problem for Children and Problem for Dogs, and its tags include #poisonous, #problem for children, #problem for dogs, #problem for cats, #contact dermatitis and #poisonous if ingested; the Problem for Cats and Problem for Dogs values and tags are the only cat/dog scoping and are what support toxic_to_pets=true. NC State's Plant Type field lists Ground Cover, Herbaceous Perennial and Poisonous. RHS's Potentially harmful field reads "Humans/Pets: IRRITANT to skin/eye; harmful if eaten. Wear gloves and other protective equipment when handling." and names no cat or dog. The two sources agree on the hazard; only NC State gives a severity rating.
unknowns: Missouri Botanical Garden and plantfinder.mobot.org pages could not be loaded (ConnectError / proxy denial); MoBot's page found for this plant is titled Euphorbia polychroma and the only epithymoides entry is a cultivar page, so neither is a dedicated page for this exact name and neither was used.

outdoor_sun_exposure is full_sun only: RHS's Position field lists Full sun only and its cultivation text says the plant 'performs best in full sun, although will adapt to partial shade'; NC State's Light field lists Full sun and Partial Shade but tags '#partial shade tolerant'. NC State's prose says 'This plant does well in full sun to partial shade' and 'Afternoon shade is beneficial during southern summers', but warns 'too much shade can cause the plant to become leggy and lose the cushion shape it is known for.' part_shade is left out as a close call, following the b111 Pineapple Sage precedent.

RHS Max Height is 0.1-0.5 metres and Max Spread 0.5-1 metres (3.9-19.7 in and 19.7-39.4 in); the NC State Dimensions block (1 ft. 0 in. - 1 ft. 6 in. for both) is used as the anchor because this species has its own NC State page.
No watering statement or structured moisture field was found; NC State and RHS give only drought-tolerance traits, so water_regime and all interval fields are null.

soil_drainage is moderate from NC State's Good Drainage + Moist + Occasionally Dry tags and RHS's 'Moist but well-drained or Well-drained'. NC State's prose prefers loose, well-drained sandy to gravelly soil.
Soil pH: NC State tags Acid, Alkaline and Neutral and RHS lists Acid or Alkaline or Neutral; open-ended bands, so no min/max set.

No source states an indoor houseplant use (NC State tags it container plant, patio), so is_houseplant is false: NC State's Plant Type field lists Ground Cover, Herbaceous Perennial and Poisonous and its USDA zones are 4a-8b. No temperature, humidity, light-fc, fertilizer or chill-damage figures were found in admissible sources.
direct_sun_hours_max left null: NC State's only hour figures come from its generic light-category legend.
is_edible is false because NC State says all parts are toxic if ingested and RHS says harmful if eaten; no source describes any edible use.

NC State's Poison block and severity rating are human-scoped; RHS's pet mention is unscoped (names no cat or dog). Only NC State's Problem for Cats and Problem for Dogs tags scope the toxicity to cats and dogs.

NC State attracts_pollinators: the page has no Attracts field and no pollinator text; support is RHS's 'Plants for pollinators' badge only, an image badge whose alt text is the label (the form the corpus cites in 46 landed files).

records.name_note: Sources split on the lead common name. NC State's rendered Common Name(s) list reads Bowman’s Root then Culver's Root (alphabetical order), while its Description opens with Culver's Root; MoBot's Noteworthy Characteristics prose says 'commonly called Culver's root'; RHS's dedicated page subtitle is Culver's root and its Other common names field lists Bowman's root among others. Culver's Root is used. RHS lists Veronica virginica as a synonym of this species.
unknowns: toxic_to_pets and toxicity_detail left null: none of the three admissible dedicated pages (NC State, MoBot, RHS) carries a Poison block, a Problem for Cats/Dogs tag, or any statement that the plant is poisonous to cats, dogs or any animal. The only related text is medicinal-use history: NC State's Uses (Ethnobotany) says the Cherokee, Iroquois, Chippewa and Menominee used the plant as an analgesic, cathartic (accelerated defecation), emetic (induces vomiting), and for coughs, fevers, rheumatism and childbirth; MoBot says 'Root has been used medicinally as a cathartic.' These are historical medicinal uses, not a toxicity finding for pets or people, and no dose or plant-part toxicity scope is given beyond MoBot's 'Root'. The root's purgative history is a reason for caution but is not recorded as a toxicity claim.
is_edible left null: no admissible source says any part is grown or used for food; the cathartic/emetic uses are medicinal, not food.

is_houseplant false: all sources treat it as an in-ground native herbaceous perennial for borders, meadows and rain gardens; none addresses indoor culture. NC State's Plant Type field lists Herbaceous Perennial, Native Plant and Wildflower.

outdoor_sun_exposure lists only full_sun: NC State's structured Light field and MoBot's Sun field both say full sun. RHS also lists Partial shade (Position: Full sun, Partial shade) and MoBot's culture text says it 'Tolerates light shade' as a conditional aside; because the two North American structured fields give full sun only, part_sun/part_shade is left out and disclosed here.
direct_sun_hours_max left null: the only hour figure is the generic NC State light-category legend wording, not species-specific prose.

soil_ph_min and soil_ph_max left null: NC State ticks Acid (<6.0), Alkaline (>8.0) and Neutral (6.0-8.0), all open-ended or spanning, and RHS says pH Acid or Alkaline or Neutral, so no bound is supportable.

soil_drainage moderate: NC State Good Drainage + Occasionally Wet, MoBot 'average, medium to wet, well-drained soil', RHS Moisture 'Moist but well-drained'. NC State also tags Wet Soil under Resistance To Challenges and MoBot lists Tolerate: Wet Soil, but no source demands standing wetness, so fast and moisture_retentive were both rejected.

water_regime keep_moist rests on MoBot's sentence 'Soils should not be allowed to dry out.' Counterpoints: MoBot's structured Water field reads 'Medium to wet' (mid-to-wet scale, not a watering instruction) and NC State describes 'average, medium to wet soil'. RHS's Cultivation line ('moist soil') was not used because it may be genus-level boilerplate shared with sibling Veronicastrum pages. No numeric watering interval is given by any source; day-interval and dry-down fields left null for an in-ground perennial.

fertilize fields, temperature, humidity, light_fc and chill_damage_f left null: no admissible source gives a figure for this species (RHS H7 is a hardiness rating, not a damage onset).
